taxonomy.note: Accepted by Kew as Salvia coccinea Buc'hoz ex Etl.; Salvia coccinea L.f. is a later illegitimate homonym and should not be treated as a separate learner taxon.

evidence: Hays — Wildflower Center printable Hays County native list (verified Hays County Natives source tab).
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly lists Salvia coccinea.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County treatment.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Source-pool membership and iNaturalist counts were not used by themselves as proof.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with leaf shape and petiole before flower color: broad triangular to ovate/deltoid serrate leaves on conspicuous petioles. Then confirm the verticillate inflorescence and long bilabiate corolla.
diagnostic_traits: opposite decussate broad triangular/ovate-deltoid serrate leaves

confusers.separator: Both can be red-flowered, but S. coccinea is generally taller with broad deltoid/ovate leaves and conspicuous petioles.
S. azurea has narrow linear-lanceolate leaves and a much taller, more open flowering axis.

candidate_sources.roles: habit; flowers; inflorescence; developing fruits; leaf arrangement
